stem: When evaluating a child for a potential primary immunodeficiency, what is the purpose of testing 'functional antibodies' like those for tetanus or diphtheria?

options.text: To determine if the child's immune system can effectively respond to a known challenge.
To check if the child has received their scheduled immunizations.
To identify specific genetic mutations in the immunoglobulin heavy chain.
To screen for the presence of maternal antibodies in an infant.

explanation: Measuring titers after vaccination shows whether the B-cells and T-cells can work together to produce a specific, lasting antibody response.
rationale: This test moves beyond just counting the number of antibodies to seeing if they actually work following a vaccine.

optionExplanations.A: Measuring titers after vaccination shows whether the B-cells and T-cells can work together to produce a specific, lasting antibody response.
optionExplanations.B: The test measures the biological response to the vaccine, not just the administrative fact of whether the vaccine was given.
optionExplanations.C: Functional testing looks at the output of the immune system; genetic mutations are identified through DNA sequencing.
optionExplanations.D: In older children (like the 18-month-old in the case study), these tests are meant to evaluate the child's own active immunity.

source.hint: This test moves beyond just counting the number of antibodies to seeing if they actually work following a vaccine.
